## Summary

| | |
|---|---|
| **Contributor** | Srishti Dutta ([\@srishtiii28](https://github.com/srishtiii28)) |
| **Organization** | The R Project for Statistical Computing |
| **Mentor** | Christophe Regouby ([\@cregouby](https://github.com/cregouby)) |
| **Repositories** | [mlverse/torchvision](https://github.com/mlverse/torchvision), [mlverse/torchvisionlib](https://github.com/mlverse/torchvisionlib) |

The work spans two packages. In **torchvision**, an R port of PyTorch's vision
library, I added the LW-DETR family of real-time detection transformers and
built out the `item_transform_*` family — augmentations that transform a whole
dataset item so that the image and its target (bounding boxes or segmentation
masks) stay aligned. In **torchvisionlib**, which supplies compiled ops to
torchvision, I contributed two native operators: the multi-scale deformable
attention kernel that LW-DETR's decoder depends on, and rotated-box IoU.

---

## Merged pull requests

### 1. Fix `draw_keypoints()` documentation and error message typo

[mlverse/torchvision#296](https://github.com/mlverse/torchvision/pull/296) ·
merged 25 March 2026 · +19 −7 across 3 files

My first contribution to the package. Three documentation defects in
`R/vision_utils.R`: the `connectivity` parameter was annotated as a `Vector`
when it accepts a `list(c(i, j), ...)` of pairs and carried a stale
"currently unavailable" note; the `colors` parameter had two copy-paste errors
carried over from `draw_bounding_boxes()` (`"boxes"` for `"keypoints"`, and
`"viridis"` for `"rainbow"` — the function calls `grDevices::rainbow()`); and an
error message read `"but is current shape is"`. Fixed at the roxygen2 source,
with `man/draw_keypoints.Rd` regenerated.

### 2. Dispatch NMS to `torchvisionlib::ops_nms()` when available

[mlverse/torchvision#325](https://github.com/mlverse/torchvision/pull/325) ·
merged 10 June 2026 · +45 −4 across 4 files ·
closes [#321](https://github.com/mlverse/torchvision/issues/321),
[#322](https://github.com/mlverse/torchvision/issues/322)

Non-maximum suppression ran in pure R on every inference call for all four
FasterRCNN variants and both MaskRCNN variants, and it dominated their runtime.
`nms()` now dispatches to the native C++ `torchvisionlib::ops_nms()` when
torchvisionlib is installed, keeping the pure R path as a fallback so behaviour
is unchanged for users without it.

Measured on a 520×520 image on CPU:

| Model | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| `model_fasterrcnn_mobilenet_v3_large_320_fpn` | ~25 s / image | ~2 s / image |
| `model_maskrcnn_resnet50_fpn` | ~1.7 min / image | ~25 s / image |

FasterRCNN went from unusable for interactive work to responsive. Tests cover
both the native dispatch and the fallback.

### 3. Add LW-DETR object detection models

[mlverse/torchvision#334](https://github.com/mlverse/torchvision/pull/334) ·
merged 4 July 2026 · +1,419 −6 across 13 files ·
closes [#328](https://github.com/mlverse/torchvision/issues/328)

An implementation of [LW-DETR](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.03459), a real-time
detection transformer, exposed as `model_lw_detr_tiny()`,
`model_lw_detr_small()`, `model_lw_detr_medium()` and `model_lw_detr_large()`
with COCO-pretrained weights. The architecture is a ViT backbone, a C2f
multi-scale projector, and a two-stage deformable-attention decoder. All four
variants load the official weights with exact key and shape match and reproduce
reference detections; `pixel_mask` is supported so letterboxed non-square inputs
work correctly.

This replaced an earlier attempt in
[#332](https://github.com/mlverse/torchvision/pull/332), which I closed in
favour of a rewrite after review.

### 4. Preallocate lists and vectors before iteration loops

[mlverse/torchvision#341](https://github.com/mlverse/torchvision/pull/341) ·
merged 20 July 2026 · +154 −170 across 15 files ·
closes [#335](https://github.com/mlverse/torchvision/issues/335)

A package-wide cleanup. Lists grown one element at a time reallocate on every
iteration; where the final length is known before the loop they are now
allocated with `vector("list", n)` and assigned by index. `folder_make_dataset()`
and the Cityscapes image collection gather into a preallocated list and
`unlist()` once rather than calling `c()` per iteration. Touches fifteen model
and dataset files.

### 5. Multi-scale deformable attention CUDA op

[mlverse/torchvisionlib#33](https://github.com/mlverse/torchvisionlib/pull/33) ·
merged 1 August 2026 · +2,136 −29 across 26 files ·
fixes [#25](https://github.com/mlverse/torchvisionlib/issues/25)

`ops_ms_deform_attn()`, the multi-scale deformable attention operator LW-DETR's
decoder cross-attention requires, replacing the slow pure-R `grid_sample`
fallback on GPU. The largest single contribution of the summer: CUDA and CPU
kernels, the autograd binding, the C++ export plumbing on both the `csrc/` and
`src/` sides, `.def` export files, Rcpp bindings, and the R-CMD-check workflow.

### 6. `item_transform_affine()` and `target_transform_affine()`

[mlverse/torchvision#367](https://github.com/mlverse/torchvision/pull/367) ·
merged 10 August 2026 · +684 across 15 files ·
closes [#347](https://github.com/mlverse/torchvision/issues/347)

Applies an affine transformation — rotation, translation, scale and shear — to
a whole dataset item, keeping the target aligned with the image. Covers
detection and segmentation items and their datasets, following the S3-dispatch
convention set out in
[#343](https://github.com/mlverse/torchvision/issues/343), the umbrella issue
tracking `item_transform_` coverage against PyTorch's `transforms.v2`.

### 7. Extend `item_transform_rotate()` to segmentation

[mlverse/torchvision#379](https://github.com/mlverse/torchvision/pull/379) ·
merged 10 August 2026 · +115 −10 across 5 files ·
closes [#363](https://github.com/mlverse/torchvision/issues/363)

Adds `item_transform_rotate.image_with_segmentation_mask()` and
`item_transform_rotate.dataset()`, so masks rotate alongside the image using
nearest-neighbour sampling — which matters because masks hold discrete class
labels that interpolation would corrupt. Detection items still return
`image_with_rotated_box` with boxes in `xyxyr` format; segmentation items keep
their class.

### 8. Add `ops_box_iou_rotated()`

[mlverse/torchvisionlib#34](https://github.com/mlverse/torchvisionlib/pull/34) ·
merged 17 August 2026 · +801 −1 across 23 files ·
fixes [#31](https://github.com/mlverse/torchvisionlib/issues/31)

IoU between rotated boxes on CPU, accepting the `cxcywhr`, `xywhr` and
`xyxyxyxy` formats. Rotated-box IoU needs polygon clipping rather than the
axis-aligned rectangle intersection that ordinary IoU uses, so this is a
genuinely separate kernel rather than a variation on `ops_nms()`.

## Open pull requests

### `item_transform_resize()`

[mlverse/torchvision#380](https://github.com/mlverse/torchvision/pull/380) ·
opened 9 August 2026 · +363 across 13 files ·
closes [#362](https://github.com/mlverse/torchvision/issues/362) ·
**changes requested**

Resizing for detection items and datasets and for segmentation items and
datasets. Boxes are rescaled by the factors actually applied to the image
rather than the requested ones, which matters when aspect ratio is preserved;
masks resize with nearest-neighbour sampling so their discrete values survive.

### `item_transform_random_resize_crop()`

[mlverse/torchvision#386](https://github.com/mlverse/torchvision/pull/386) ·
opened 11 August 2026 · +556 −3 across 9 files ·
closes [#361](https://github.com/mlverse/torchvision/issues/361) ·
**changes requested**

The random resized crop augmentation across all four item kinds: object
detection item and dataset, semantic segmentation item and dataset. Includes a
fix keeping the central-crop fallback inside the image bounds.

### `item_transform_random_affine()`

[mlverse/torchvision#390](https://github.com/mlverse/torchvision/pull/390) ·
opened 14 August 2026 · +458 −48 across 9 files ·
closes [#354](https://github.com/mlverse/torchvision/issues/354) ·
**awaiting review**

Random affine for detection items, segmentation items and their datasets,
drawing rotation, translation, scale and shear once per item so image and
target stay aligned. Also fixes a bug in the existing
`transform_random_affine()`: given a bare number for `shear`, it widened
`degrees` instead of `shear`, leaving the shear range incomplete and making
sampling fail.

### `object_detection_dataset` and `object_detection_target` S3 classes

[mlverse/torchvision#391](https://github.com/mlverse/torchvision/pull/391) ·
opened 19 August 2026 · +174 −26 across 21 files ·
closes [#364](https://github.com/mlverse/torchvision/issues/364) ·
**awaiting review**

A structural change rather than a new feature. Detection datasets now carry an
`object_detection_dataset` class and their item target `y` an
`object_detection_target` class, so target transforms dispatch on class instead
of inspecting the target's fields. Touches the COCO and Pascal VOC datasets and
the six RF100 collections.
